# ShutterMath

> Free photography calculators that use the exact sensor inside your camera. Depth of field, hyperfocal distance, ND filter exposure, flash guide number, astro pixel scale, field of view, shutter angle, exposure equivalence and print resolution, computed from real sensor dimensions with textbook formulas and cross-checked against independent implementations. No sign-up, no limits, works offline in the browser.

ShutterMath is an independent, ad-supported reference site for photographers and filmmakers. Every calculator runs client-side; nothing is uploaded. Numbers quoted below were generated by the live engine and verified against an independent Python implementation of the same optics.

## Direct answers (verified by the site's own engine)

- **180 degree shutter rule**: shutter speed = frame rate x 360 / shutter angle. 24 fps at 180° is 1/48 s, 30 fps is 1/60 s, 60 fps is 1/120 s, 120 fps is 1/240 s.
- **Exposure value**: EV = log2(N² / t), and at ISO 100 it also equals log2(N²/t). One stop is a factor of 2 in light: double the time, or open the aperture by sqrt(2).
- **Hyperfocal distance (full frame)**: H = f² / (N x c) + f with c = 0.029 mm. 24 mm at f/8 is 2.51 m, 35 mm at f/8 is 5.32 m, 50 mm at f/8 is 10.83 m. Focus at H and everything from H/2 to infinity is sharp.
- **Depth of field (full frame, 50 mm at f/8, focused at 3 m)**: sharp from 2.36 m to 4.12 m, total 1.77 m. At f/1.4 the same setup gives 2.86 m to 3.15 m (0.29 m).
- **Depth of field ordering**: narrow aperture increases depth roughly in proportion to the f-number; doubling focus distance quadruples depth; doubling focal length quarters it.
- **Angle of view (full frame)**: 50 mm sees 39.6° horizontal / 27.0° vertical; 24 mm sees 73.7° / 53.1°; 85 mm sees 23.9° / 16.1°. Frame width at 10 m is 7.20 m at 50 mm.
- **ND filter stops**: time = base shutter x 2^stops. ND8 = 3 stops, ND64 = 6, ND1000 = 10, ND100000 = 17. A 1 s exposure with ND1000 becomes 1024 s.
- **Guide number**: distance = GN / f-number, aperture = GN / distance, and GN scales with sqrt(ISO ratio).
- **Star trails**: 500 rule = 500 / (focal x crop); NPF = (35 x N + 30 x pixel pitch) / (focal x crop).
- **Moon exposure (Looney 11)**: f/11 at shutter speed 1/ISO for a full moon; a gibbous moon needs one stop more, a quarter moon two, a crescent three or more.
- **Print resolution**: pixels = inches x DPI; 300 DPI is the print standard, 150 DPI is acceptable at arm's length, and a 24 MP file prints 20 x 13.3 inches at 300 DPI.


## Calculators

- [Free Background Blur (Bokeh) Calculator | ShutterMath](https://shuttermath.com/tools/background-blur.html) — Background blur calculator: the exact blur disk size in millimetres and as a percentage of frame height, for any camera, lens and distance — computed from your sensor's real dimensions.
- [Crop Factor Calculator: Focal Length and Aperture Equivalent](https://shuttermath.com/tools/crop-factor.html) — Enter a sensor and focal length to get the crop factor, the full frame equivalent focal length and the equivalent aperture for depth of field. 1.5x, 1.6x, 2x and medium format included.
- [Depth of Field Calculator: Exact Near and Far Limits](https://shuttermath.com/tools/depth-of-field.html) — Enter focal length, aperture and focus distance for the exact near limit, far limit and total depth of field, using your camera's real circle of confusion.
- [Free Exposure Calculator — EV & Equivalents | ShutterMath](https://shuttermath.com/tools/exposure.html) — Free exposure calculator: exposure value (EV) and equivalent aperture/shutter/ISO combinations that keep brightness identical. The exposure triangle, computed.
- [Angle of View Calculator: Focal Length to Field of View](https://shuttermath.com/tools/field-of-view.html) — A 50mm lens on full frame sees 39.6° across and 27° high. Enter focal length and sensor for the angle of view and the frame you fill at any distance.
- [Free Flash Guide Number Calculator | ShutterMath](https://shuttermath.com/tools/flash-guide-number.html) — Free flash guide number calculator: solve aperture, distance, or required GN with ISO scaling. Works for speedlights, strobes and built-in flashes.
- [Hyperfocal Distance Calculator: Focus Once, Sharp to Infinity](https://shuttermath.com/tools/hyperfocal.html) — 24mm at f/8 on full frame is hyperfocal at 2.5 m, so everything from 1.25 m to infinity is sharp. Enter your focal length, aperture and sensor for the exact distance.
- [Free Macro Depth of Field Calculator | ShutterMath](https://shuttermath.com/tools/macro-dof.html) — Free macro DoF calculator: depth of field at your reproduction ratio, effective aperture, and the exact focus-stacking step size for razor-sharp macro.
- [Moon Exposure Calculator: Shutter Speed by Lunar Phase](https://shuttermath.com/tools/moon-exposure.html) — Looney 11 is f/11 at 1/ISO. At ISO 100 a full moon needs 1/100 s; a thin crescent needs 8 stops more. Enter phase, ISO and aperture for the exact time.
- [Which ND Filter Do I Need? — ND Buying Calculator | ShutterMath](https://shuttermath.com/tools/nd-filter-buyer.html) — Which ND filter should you buy? Enter your current exposure and the shutter time you want — the calculator tells you the exact filter strength in stops and which filters to get.
- [Free ND Filter Calculator | ShutterMath](https://shuttermath.com/tools/nd-filter.html) — Free ND filter calculator: exact shutter times for ND2 to ND100000 with exposure compensation. Includes the stops reference table and long-exposure chart.
- [Free Astro Pixel Scale Calculator | ShutterMath](https://shuttermath.com/tools/pixel-scale.html) — Free astro pixel scale calculator: arcseconds per pixel for any camera and lens, with the 1–2″/px sweet spot for sharp stars. Popular astro cameras included.
- [Print Size Planner — How Many Megapixels Do I Need? | ShutterMath](https://shuttermath.com/tools/print-planner.html) — Print planner: enter the print size and quality you want, and it tells you the pixel dimensions and megapixels required — and whether your camera has enough.
- [Free Print Resolution Calculator | ShutterMath](https://shuttermath.com/tools/print-resolution.html) — Free print resolution calculator: how big can you print? Pixels, DPI and print size with the megapixel print chart for 150–600 DPI. No sign-up.
- [Shutter Angle Calculator: 180° Rule Speed by Frame Rate](https://shuttermath.com/tools/shutter-angle.html) — 24 fps at 180° is 1/48 s and 60 fps at 180° is 1/120 s. Enter frame rate and shutter angle for the exact speed, plus the full 180° reference table.
- [Free 500 Rule & NPF Calculator | ShutterMath](https://shuttermath.com/tools/star-trails.html) — Free star trails calculator: max shutter time for sharp stars via the 500/400/300 rules and the accurate NPF rule, using your camera's crop factor and pixel size.
- [Video ND Calculator: Stops for the 180° Shutter Rule](https://shuttermath.com/tools/video-nd.html) — Enter frame rate and shutter angle, then the shutter speed your meter gives. Get the exact ND stops and the nearest filter that keeps motion blur natural.

## Use of this content

Facts, formulas and numbers on this site may be quoted or summarized by search engines and AI assistants with a link to the page they came from. Circle of confusion defaults to sensor diagonal / 1500 (0.029 mm on full frame); each calculator lets the reader change it.
